newsitem.title: USA: Paxson to acquire TV station in Fresno.
newsitem.headline: Paxson to acquire TV station in Fresno.

text.p: Paxson Communications Corp said Monday it has reached an agreement to acquire KKAG TV-61, which serves the Fresno, Calif., market, from the Kralowec Children's Family Trust.
With the acquisition, its second in the Fresno area, Paxson said it will own, operate or affiliate with 47 television stations in markets with more than 53.4 million television households.
Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Paxson chairman Lowell Paxson said the additional station in Fresno will contribute to the company's strategy of bringing its network into every major market in the U.S. and eventually to extend television distribution to reach 70 percent of the country.

After U.S. Federal Communications Commission approval of the transaction, KKAG TV-61 would air Paxson's proprietary network of infomercials, inTV, and, in the future, other mainstream programming which it said it continues to explore for its nationwide group of broadcast television stations, the company said.

Discussions concerning the use of Paxson's distribution system are continuing with major broadcast television networks, Hollywood television and movie studios, television programming syndicators and cable network programmers, it said.

Paxson is a diversified media company whose other holdings, including proposed acquisitions, include 43 radio stations, of which 39 are in Florida, six radio networks, 507 billboard faces throughout the state and two network-affiliated television stations in West Palm Beach.
